IntelliProve raises €2.7 million to develop camera-based robot vital-sign sensing

The seed round supports expansion from apps to robots alongside more data and clinical validation, rather than a new medical-device authorization.

Humanoids Daily ↗18 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

Expanding beyond applications

Belgian company IntelliProve announced €2.7 million in seed financing led by Miles Ahead, with Wit-Gele Kruis, imec.istart and angel investors participating, in reporting published around November 18–19. The company aims to extend camera-based vital-sign sensing into humanoids and assistive robots.

Signals from skin color and breathing

Remote photoplethysmography analyzes small pulse-related skin-color changes and breathing movements during an approximately 30-second face scan. The company offers estimates of heart rate, variability, breathing and blood pressure. Pressure is inferred by a model rather than measured with a cuff; lighting and motion are important evaluation conditions.

Validation remains part of the funded work

Funding will broaden population and operating-condition data, benchmark readings against reference methods and support work toward Class IIa certification under EU medical-device rules. Robotics partners remain unnamed and full blood-pressure validation has not been published. The described workflow passes readings to carers rather than letting a robot decide treatment independently.
